title: Typhoon
local: Dampas: severe wind is the main risk. Rare 500-year winds can reach 117 to 220 kph.
before: Charge phones and power banks. Fill water containers.
Tie down or bring in anything the wind can throw.
Know your evacuation centre and how to get there.
Pack the go-bag with medicines, IDs and a flashlight.
during: Stay inside, away from windows and doors.
Do not go out in the eye of the storm. The wind returns fast.
Follow PAGASA bulletins on a battery radio or your phone.
Leave early if officials tell you to evacuate.
after: Stay away from fallen lines and flooded roads.
Boil or treat drinking water until it is declared safe.
Check on neighbours, older people and children.
Take photos of damage before you clean up.

title: Earthquake
local: Dampas: ground shaking is rated Intensity VIII (prone). The nearest active fault is about 12.4 km away.
before: Fix tall shelves and heavy frames to the wall.
Pick a safe spot in each room, under a sturdy table.
Practise drop, cover and hold on with the whole family.
Know the high ground nearest to you.
during: Drop to your hands and knees. Cover your head and neck. Hold on.
Stay where you are until the shaking stops.
If you are outside, move away from walls, poles and wires.
If you are near the coast and the shaking is strong or long, move to high ground at once.
after: Expect aftershocks. Drop, cover and hold on again.
Check for injuries and fires. Use a flashlight, not a flame.
Switch off power and gas if you smell gas or see damage.
Text instead of calling to keep lines free.

title: Flood
local: Dampas: flood hazard is not confirmed yet. Ask the barangay and watch the rainfall warnings.
before: Learn which nearby streets flood first.
Keep documents and medicines in a waterproof bag, up high.
PAGASA rainfall warnings: yellow means be alert, orange means be ready to evacuate, red means evacuate now.
during: Move to higher ground early. Do not wait for water at the door.
Never walk or drive through moving flood water.
Switch off power at the main if water is entering the house.
after: Do not eat food touched by flood water.
Clean and dry everything. Mud and damp bring sickness.
Watch for fever, diarrhoea or skin wounds, and see a health worker.

title: Tsunami
local: Dampas: HazardHunterPH lists tsunami as Safe for the pin. Strong shaking near the coast still means go to high ground.
before: Know the nearest high ground and the way on foot.
Learn the natural warnings: strong or long shaking, the sea suddenly pulling back or rising, a loud roar.
during: Move to high ground at once. Do not wait for a message.
Go on foot. Roads jam quickly.
Stay up until officials say it is safe. Waves can keep coming for hours.
after: Stay away from the shore until it is declared safe.
Avoid damaged buildings and flooded areas.
Check on family at your meeting place.

title: Fire
before: Fit a smoke alarm if you can, and test it every month.
Keep two exits clear. Agree a meeting spot outside.
Never leave cooking, candles or chargers unattended.
during: Get out first. Crawl low under smoke.
Do not go back inside for belongings.
Call 911 from a safe place.
after: Do not re-enter until firefighters say so.
Tell the barangay and your family where you are.
Seek medical care for burns and smoke.

title: Heat
before: Check the PAGASA heat index each morning.
Plan outdoor work for early morning or late afternoon.
Keep water and oral rehydration salts at home.
during: Drink water often, before you feel thirsty.
Rest in the shade or a cool room. Wear light clothes.
Never leave a child, older person or pet in a parked car.
after: Watch for headache, dizziness, cramps or hot dry skin.
Cool the person down and seek care if they do not recover fast.

title: Landslide
local: Dampas: rain-induced landslide is rated Low at the pin.
before: Learn if your home sits under or on a slope.
Watch for new cracks, leaning trees or muddy water from a slope.
Agree a place to go when heavy rain lasts for days.
during: Leave at once if you hear rumbling or see the ground move.
Move sideways, away from the path, not downhill along it.
Do not cross bridges or rivers swollen by rain.
after: Stay away from the slide area. More can follow.
Report trapped people to rescue teams. Do not dig alone.
Watch for broken water, power and gas lines.
